# A duty run that has held the lock past two tick boundaries: alive, ticking,
# and doing nothing. The floor calls this STUCK, and it is the state a healthy
# fleet never produces on demand.
ff-stuck       running  stuck
# Reachable, has ticked before, and its crontab holds no live tick.sh line —
# `crew hire` before it arms, a hand-disarmed box, and EVERY drill box by
# design (drill/rehearsal.sh disarms before any tick). It read SILENT for five
# consecutive drill runs, which is an alarm nobody could act on (#189).
ff-disarmed    running  disarmed
# Hired, armed, credentials never rejected — and no ~/duty/duty.log at all,
# because the engine has not run once. The credential columns must read
# `waiting`, not `stale`: this box has not STOPPED ticking, it has not STARTED
# (#265). Its CLI twin is cli-neverticked in fixtures/cli-fleet.txt.
ff-neverticked running  neverticked
# Healthy boxes whose guest clocks differ from the collector by three hours.
ff-skew-behind running  skew-behind
ff-skew-ahead  running  skew-ahead
ff-invalid-age running  invalid-tickage
ff-missing-age running  missing-tickage
ff-silent-behind running skew-silent-behind
ff-silent-ahead  running skew-silent-ahead
# Two healthy, ticking boxes that differ only in what their engine files hash
# to (#159, #190). `modified` is the failure that instrument exists to catch —
# a hotfix nobody told the fleet about, on a box whose every other reading is
# fine — and `unverified` is the state every box is in on the day content
# stamping ships. Both must render as themselves on the tile; a page that shows
# either as a verified engine has added a word and no information.
ff-modified    running  modified
ff-unverified  running  unverified
# #610 — STUCK is measured against the ceiling the in-flight session declares,
# not against a fleet-wide 600s. All three run the SAME evidence: a `build`
# session in flight saying `timeout=3600s`. They differ only in how long the
# lock has been held — 40 minutes, the bound exactly (ceiling + the 60s kill
# grace), and one second past it — so a reader comparing against anything but
# that line grades at least one of them wrong. The first is @danmt's report:
# under the old rule it wore the pulsing badge, and the badge hides the
# running-session panel it should have been showing.
ff-lane-build  running  lane-build
ff-lane-edge   running  lane-edge
ff-lane-over   running  lane-over
# A session in flight whose START carries no `timeout=` token at all — every
# line written by an engine older than #538. Nothing on the record to read a
# ceiling from, so this box falls back to STUCK_AFTER_S and must be graded and
# worded exactly as it is today.
ff-lane-legacy running  lane-legacy
# The same build-in-flight evidence, but the probe reports NO lock: the
# evidence poll saw nothing to grade, and only the 10s heartbeat has an age
# (3661s). The one box that drives the verdict through fleet.py's ping-tier
# overlay rather than through build_unit, which is how #610's "one decision
# function, asserted from both entry points" is actually proved — the note it
# reaches must be byte-identical to ff-lane-over's.
ff-lane-ping   running  lane-ping
